title: Canary probe for streaming + function-call compatibility with version-pinned onboarded models
creator: Amina Patel
description: Create and run a lightweight canary probe and automated verification harness that validates streaming semantics and function/tool-calling behavior for newly onboarded models when pinned to specific versions. The probe should exercise edge cases for partial tokens, interrupted streams, tool call injection, and version-fallback behavior, and publish a distilled performance profile (latency, token throughput, error-mode fingerprints) to the model catalog for the onboarded version.
background: We onboard multiple open and partner models weekly. Past incidents show discrepancies between model-level streaming semantics and Redwood's streaming + function-calling runtime (e.g., truncated tool call payloads, inconsistent finalization events, or divergent tokenization under quantized kernels). Model owners also want a deterministic way to pin a version and see a published performance profile before enabling production traffic. Current onboarding flow lacks an automated canary that combines functional compatibility checks and perf sampling under the pinned-version constraint.
goals: Provide an automated canary probe that runs as part of model onboarding and when a model version is pinned
Detect regressions in streaming behavior and function/tool call semantics before models are marked production-ready
Produce and publish a concise performance profile for the pinned model version: p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, and observed error modes
Integrate probe outputs into the onboarding checklist and surface failures in Console and onboarding dashboards
acceptance_criteria: Probe runs as a gated step in the onboarding pipeline when a version is pinned and returns pass/fail within configured timeout
Probe verifies: continuous streaming sequence (including preempted reconnects), function/tool-call start/end markers, and correct structured payloads emitted by tool calls
Probe produces a JSON summary with latency percentiles, throughput, and a small set of observed failure fingerprints that is saved to the model catalog and linked in the onboarding ticket
Failures generate an automated jira/linear follow-up with logs, request/response traces, and suggested mitigations
Console displays a 'compatibility certification' badge for pinned versions that pass the probe and a failure reason for those that do not
implementation_plan: Design probe spec: test vectors (streaming prompts, long prefix + continuation, forced reconnect, multi-tool call sequences with nested arguments)
Extend existing verification harness (ENG-30177) with a new probe runner that accepts model://<name>@<version> and runtime config (quantization mode, kernel flags)
Add instrumentation hooks to capture token boundaries, SSE events, and function-call structured payloads at high fidelity
Implement perf sampling: execute N concurrent short sessions (configurable), collect token latencies and aggregate to p50/p95
Write uploader that writes the distilled profile to model-catalog API and triggers onboarding pipeline callback
Wire probe as a pre-release gating step in onboarding CI and add Console display integration
test_plan: Unit tests for probe runner and synthetic stream generator
End-to-end tests against a local mock runtime that can simulate partial-send and reconnect scenarios
Canary: run probe against 3 recently onboarded internal models (small/medium/large) with pinned versions and verify results
Chaos scenarios: drop TCP for brief windows, force GC pauses on the runtime node to validate probe sensitivity
Manual review: PM/Design to verify Console badge wording and failure states
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge probe into verification-harness main behind feature flag; run nightly for new onboarded versions
Step 2: Enable gating on non-critical test customers (internal + opt-in partners)
Step 3: Flip gating to block 'certification' label for production onboarding once stable for two weeks
Step 4: Publish documentation and onboarding checklist updates; run training session for SREs and model-onboarding engineers

decisions: Use a small deterministic set of prompts for canary to keep runtime costs bounded and produce comparable perf profiles
Treat function-call payload integrity as a hard failure (not a warning) for certification
Publish only a distilled performance profile to the catalog (no raw per-request traces stored long-term) to limit data volume
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Probe false-positives caused by transient infra noise. Mitigation: require 2 failing runs within 24h before blocking certification
Risk: High cost if probe runs at large scale. Mitigation: sample small N sessions and cap parallelism per onboarding
Risk: Different quantization/kernel combos produce divergent behavior. Mitigation: run probe for the primary runtime config that the model will be served on and record the config in profile
notes: This ticket focuses on the compatibility proof and perf profile publishing. Follow-up tickets will cover automated remediation suggestions and richer regression alerting tied to prompt-based evals.
